item.title: [BOOKKEEPER-632] AutoRecovery should consider read only bookies
item.description:
Autorecovery Auditor should consider the readonly bookies as Available Bookies while publishing the under-replicated ledgers.

Also AutoRecoveryDaemon should shutdown if the local bookie is readonly
item.summary: AutoRecovery should consider read only bookies

-1 the patch contains 1 line(s) with trailing spaces

Patch is having one line with trailing spaces, which is added to remove from the code.

The whitespace is actually in the comment for BookKeeperAdmin#getReadOnlyBookie. I've actually added a tool to find this, BOOKKEEPER-635. It should make this easier to find in future.

The patch adds a new public api to read the readonly bookies, then manually reads them in Auditor#getAvailableBookies(). It would be much better if this method read the bookies through BookKeeperAdmin's apis, so that if we change the format in future, we have less places to update.
Cancelling until issue addressed.
Attaching the patch for trail space removal.
This doesn't address the other issue though. Auditor should use the public api to read the readonly bookies, rather than reading from zk directly.

he patch adds a new public api to read the readonly bookies, then manually reads them in Auditor#getAvailableBookies(). It would be much better if this method read the bookies through BookKeeperAdmin's apis, so that if we change the format in future, we have less places to update.

I agree with your point Ivan, But the ways bookie addresses handled in Auditor and ReplicationWorker are different. In Auditor, bookie address is treated as just string, where as in RW its InetSocketAddress. BookKeeperAdmin#getReadOnlyBookie() will return collection of InetSocketAdress. So changes for this will be more and IMO that is out of scope of this Jira.

Any thoughts..?

InetSocketAddress can easily be converted to String with o.a.bookkeeper.util.StringUtils#addrToString. Reading directly from ZK is bad, because it's putting duplicate code in a number of places, which need to be updated if there's a change to the /ledgers/available format. For example, when /ledgers/available/readonly was added, this broke some bits of code that expected every znode under /ledgers/available to be a bookie. In fact, the code that this is fixing was guilty of this. Moving the handling of ZK to a central place prevents this situation occurring again in the future.

hey Vinay, really sorry about taking so long to get to this. Had a trip to the US last week, and previous weeks were eaten up preparing for it.

Regarding the patch, we don't want to expose zookeeper apis in our public apis, and BookKeeperAdmin#getAvailableBookies() is a public api. It would be better to add a new API, 

BookieWatcher#notifyBookiesChanged(BookiesListener listener);

interface BookiesListener {
    void availableBookiesChanged();
}

This way, BookKeeperAdmin isn't exposing anything new except for the #getReadOnlyBookies() api.

The api is clearer if waiting for notification is separated from the reading. I've attached a patch that does this.

Also, auditor shouldn't call #register on a passed in ZK object. This overwrites the previous watcher, which could lead to unpredictable behaviour. In any case, Auditor shouldn't watch for expired. It's already watched for by the watcher created in AutoRecoveryMain.

patch looks good.
Only one doubt. why we need bkc.bookieWatcher.readBookiesBlocking(); as this would have been called in BookKeeper constructor.
one more.. Patch misses BookiesListener
Posting the updated patch, on top of ikelly Patch
because the bookkeeper client is reused, and the readonly bookies may have changed, but the watcher may not have been triggered yet. It's really just to ensure we have the freshest list.
Since we are registering for the changes, bkc.bookieWatcher.readBookiesBlocking() may not be required.
